title: Andate ya
desc: Leaving a house, which takes forty minutes
setting: Nine at night at doña Carmen's. You have work at six and you have just said the word bueno.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¿Ya se van? Pero si acaban de llegar.
steps.en: Are you going already? But you have only just got here.

options.es: Ya va siendo hora, doña. Mañana entro temprano.
options.en: It is getting to be time, doña. I start early tomorrow.
options.feedback: A reason that is not about her, said after the bueno rather than instead of it. The first stage, done properly.
Correct, and about thirty minutes early. Standing up now would be abrupt.
Honest and blunt. In her front room it lands as though the evening wore you out.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Quédense otro ratito. Ahorita hago más café.
steps.en: Stay a little longer. I will make more coffee in a minute.

options.es: Un ratito más entonces, pero sin café.
options.en: A little longer then, but no coffee.
options.feedback: She insisted once, which is obligatory, and you gave her half. Now you can leave in ten minutes without anybody losing.
Accepted the whole offer. That is another forty minutes and you have work at six.

options.es: No, de verdad ya nos vamos.
options.en: No, really, we are going now.
options.feedback: Refusing the first insistence flatly is the one move that stings.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: (en el portón) Y dígale a Lucía que me llame.
steps.en: (at the gate) And tell Lucía to call me.

options.es: Yo le digo, doña. ¿Todo bien con usted?
options.en: I will tell her, doña. Is everything all right with you?
options.feedback: The gate is where the real thing gets said. You noticed and you asked.

options.en: Yes, I will let her know.
options.feedback: A message taken. The gate is where she would have told you why.

options.en: She has her own phone, doña.
options.feedback: True and cold, and it ends the one part of the evening that had something in it.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.en: Take care on the way, son.

options.es: Gracias, doña. Que pase buena noche.
options.en: Thank you, doña. Have a good night.
options.feedback: Warm, correct, and it lets both of you stop. Adiós was never an option.
Adiós from a gate you will be back at on Sunday is too big a word.
Ya me voy was thirty minutes ago. Saying it at the gate reopens the whole sequence.
